segments.he: גְּמָ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: צִיר דֶּלֶת שִׁידָּה תֵּיבָה וּמִגְדָּל, בַּמִּקְדָּשׁ — מַחֲזִירִין, בַּמְּדִינָה — דּוֹחֲקִין. וְהָעֶלְיוֹן — כָּאן וְכָאן לֹא יַחֲזִיר, גְּזֵרָה שֶׁמָּא יִתְקַע. וְאִם תָּקַע — חַיָּיב חַטָּאת.
segments.en: «GEMARA:» «The Sages taught» a baraita: With regard to the lower «hinge pin of the door of a carriage, box, or cupboard, one» may «restore» it to its place «in the Temple; in the» rest of the «country one» may only push it «back» into place, provided that it did not come out of its socket entirely. As for «the upper» hinge, «one» may «not restore» it «in either» place. This is prohibited as «a preventive measure, lest» one come to «bang» it in forcefully, thereby performing an actual labor prohibited by Torah law. «And if he» actually «banged» it in, «he is liable» to bring «a sin-offering,» as his action is considered building.

segments.he: שֶׁל בּוֹר וְשֶׁל דּוּת וְשֶׁל יָצִיעַ — לֹא יַחְזִיר, וְאִם הֶחְזִיר חַיָּיב חַטָּאת.
segments.en: With regard to the hinge pin of the door of «a pit, cistern, or an extension» to a building, «one» may «not restore» it to its place at all. «And if» one «restored» it to its place, «he is liable» to bring «a sin-offering.» The above distinction applies only to movable utensils, whereas anything attached to the ground may certainly not be fixed in place, as this is regarded as prohibited building.

moves.summary: baraita elaborating the mishna's hinge-pin rule

moves.cueHe: של בור ושל דות ושל יציע
moves.summary: doors of pits, cisterns and extensions may not be restored at all

positions.claim: lower pin restored in Temple, pushed in elsewhere; upper never, lest he bang it in; fixed structures never
